questions_and_answers.question_text: What kind of verb is shízài, and how is it most often used?
What connotation does shízài carry when used of people?
Name the four uses of méi yìsi.
What kind of ending is -xiaqu here, and what does it mean?
Which prepositional verb says what you are interested IN?
Write the Chinese for "This book is too boring. I can't read on."

answers.answer_text: Zhèiběn shū tài méi yìsi, wǒ kànbuxiaqu le.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "I really don't know."
Write the Chinese for "Go on talking. We all love to listen."

answers.answer_text: Shuōxiaqu a, wǒmen dōu ài tīng.

questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the literal meaning of méi yìsi?
Write the Chinese for "What kind of books are you most interested in?"

answers.answer_text: Nǐ duì shénmeyàngrde shū zuì yǒu xìngqù?

articles.text:
7. A: Liú Xiānshengde kè shízài    Mr. Liú's class is really boring.
      méi yìsi.
   B: Nǐ tīngxiaqu, mànmanr huì    If you keep attending it, gradually
      yǒu xìngqùde.                 you'll become interested.

Notes on No. 7

shízài: "really, indeed, honestly; to be true, to be real." This is an adjectival verb which is most often used as an ADVERB.

Wǒ shízài bù zhīdào.             I really (honestly) don't know.
Yàoshi nǐ shízài méi bànfǎ, nà   If you really can't do it, then just
jiù suàn le.                     forget it.

Shízài can also be used of PEOPLE, carrying the connotation of DEPENDABILITY:

Tā zhèige rén hěn shízài.        He is very sincere and dependable.

méi yìsi: This phrase, meaning literally "has no meaning," has an abundance of uses:

(1) UNINTERESTING, BORING
Zhèiběn shū zhēn méi yìsi.       This book is really boring.

(2) POINTLESS, MEANINGLESS
Tā bù dǒng, zài jiǎng yě méi     He doesn't understand. It's pointless
yìsi.                            to try to explain it any more.

(3) TO BE A DRAG
Tā zài Měiguo, tā àiren zài      He's in America and his love is in
Déguo, zhēn méi yìsi.            Germany. What a drag!

(4) WITHOUT VALUE, NOT WORTHY OF RESPECT
Zài tā bèihòu shuō zhèiyàngrde   Talking like that behind her back is
huà, zhēn méi yìsi!              really low.

tīngxiaqu: "to go on listening." Here xiaqu is NOT used as a directional ending, but rather as a RESULTATIVE ending, "to continue, to go on." As a resultative verb, tīngxiaqu may take de and bu as middle syllables.

Zhèiběn shū tài méi yìsi, wǒ     This book is too boring. I can't
kànbuxiaqu le.                   read on.
Shuōxiaqu a, wǒmen dōu ài tīng.  Go on talking. We all love to listen.
Nǐ zhèiyang děngxiaqu zěnme      How can you go on waiting like this?
xíng ne?

yǒu xìngqù: "to be interested." Use the prepositional verb duì to say what you are interested in.

Nǐ duì shénmeyàngrde shū zuì     What kind of books are you most
yǒu xìngqù?                      interested in?
